name: Cro-Mags
label: Victory
lede: Lower East Side squat kids, Hare Krishna devotees and a teenage drummer from the Stimulators made the record every New York hardcore band measures itself against, then spent forty years fighting, in court and once with a knife, over who owns it.

eras.title: Disco Smoothy to Cro-Mags
eras.text: Nobody agrees on when Cro-Mags started: Harley Flanagan says 1980, John Joseph says 1981. What's certain is a revolving door of Lower East Side kids, a Bad Brains roadie who found Krishna, and a bassist who'd been drumming in a punk band since he was eleven.

years.h: Harley Flanagan's first Cro-Mags plays as Disco Smoothy
years.p: By Harley Flanagan's account, the band debuted as Disco Smoothy at the Peppermint Lounge with Dave Stein on guitar, Dave Hahn on drums and John Berry singing.
years.xp:
Flanagan was born in San Francisco in 1967 and grew up on the Lower East Side. At nine he published a book of poems and drawings with a foreword by Allen Ginsberg; at eleven he was drumming for [[The Stimulators|498b08a4-b2ec-48f9-a201-1ea856a548b4]], the band of his aunt Denise Mercedes. He dropped out of school in seventh grade.

The founding date is its own feud. Flanagan's 2016 memoir Hard-Core: Life of My Own says 1980; John Joseph's 2007 book The Evolution of a Cro-Magnon says 1981. The band also went by Mode of Ignorance before settling on Cro-Mags.

years.h: John Joseph, a Bad Brains roadie, sings with Cro-Mags
years.p: John Joseph had come out of foster homes, the streets and a stint in the Navy. Working as a roadie for [[Bad Brains|e919b253-da5b-4aae-a444-6a368376a2d6]] got him into yoga, meditation and plant-based eating; in 1982 he became a Hare Krishna devotee.

years.h: Flanagan moves to drums, young Todd Youth takes bass
years.p: Harley Flanagan also helps start [[Murphy's Law|4a9fae02-7de0-4cb8-97d7-1fd790d9675e]] this year. Todd Youth, nicknamed by Bad Brains' H.R. for sneaking into the city from sixth grade on, plays bass in Cro-Mags from 1982.

years.h: Eric Casanova sings, Roger Miret plays bass, Mackie Jayson drums
years.p: Cro-Mags' line-up keeps churning: future [[Agnostic Front|40b8a690-94e4-4c82-ad0f-73f4b841e46a]] singer Roger Miret holds the bass for a year, and Mackie Jayson takes the drums.

years.h: John Joseph takes Cro-Mags' mic from Eric Casanova
years.p: Harley Flanagan returns to bass and John Joseph becomes the singer, setting up the line-up that will make The Age of Quarrel.

eras.title: The Age of Quarrel
eras.text: One album on Profile Records turned New York hardcore toward metal and toward Krishna at the same time. Parris Mayhew and Harley Flanagan wrote most of it, John Joseph sang it, and within a year he was out.

years.cap: The Age of Quarrel, Profile Records, 1986
years.h: The Age of Quarrel on Profile Records
years.p: Recorded at Eastside Studios in New York with producer Chris Williamson. The title is a translation of Kali Yuga, the Hindu age of spiritual decline.
years.xp:
Parris Mayhew has said Rush directly inspired several of the riffs. Revolver ranked the album 22nd among the greatest punk albums in 2018, and in 2024 Revolver readers voted it the greatest NYHC album ever.

[[Hatebreed|40b7efb7-1268-4a80-b354-600afdcbe9e2]]'s Jamey Jasta calls it one of the most crucial albums in hardcore history.

years.h: MTV airs Cro-Mags' We Gotta Know, stage dives and all
years.p: Parris Mayhew directed the clip. It ran on 120 Minutes and Headbangers Ball, one of the first MTV videos to show slam dancing and crowd surfing.
years.xp: [[Earth Crisis|88a6037e-87ba-492a-a54c-c927aa620cb8]] singer Karl Buechner has said the We Gotta Know video was the spark that got him into hardcore.

years.h: John Joseph is out; Harley Flanagan sings for Cro-Mags
years.p: Wikipedia lists John Joseph as expelled in 1987. Harley Flanagan takes over vocals while still playing bass.

eras.title: Crossover, and a revolving mic
eras.text: Without John Joseph, Cro-Mags went metal and toured Europe with thrash bands. Joseph came back in 1991 for two Century Media albums, and the songwriting credits became the next argument.

years.h: Best Wishes: Flanagan sings, Pete Hines drums, then flees
years.p: Recorded in a couple of days at Normandy Sound in Warren, Rhode Island. Drummer Pete Hines left mid-session, reportedly spooked by local folklore.
years.xp:
Guitarist Doug Holland was struggling with heroin addiction during the sessions, and Parris Mayhew ended up playing guitar on four of the eight songs. Mayhew has said John Joseph couldn't find a melody on the heavier new material, so the band moved on without him.

Kerrang! put Best Wishes at No. 36 on its 50 best albums of 1989, a textbook case of crossover done right.

years.h: The Down But Not Out tour, with Destruction
years.p: Cro-Mags tour Best Wishes for two months with the German thrash band Destruction as support.

years.h: John Joseph returns; Parris Mayhew leaves
years.p: John Joseph is back as Cro-Mags' singer, and co-founder Parris Mayhew departs, not to return until 1999.

years.h: Alpha Omega on Century Media, and whose songs they are
years.p: Parris Mayhew says he and Rob Buckley wrote most of Alpha Omega though neither plays on it. Harley Flanagan disputes that.

years.h: Near Death Experience, John Joseph's last Cro-Mags album
years.p: Produced by Harley Flanagan. It's the final studio appearance for both John Joseph and guitarist Doug Holland; Cro-Mags wouldn't make another album for seven years.

eras.title: Revenge, and a pile of other names
eras.text: Flanagan and Mayhew got back together with ex-Suicidal Tendencies guitarist Rocky George, made one album and fell out for good. Meanwhile rival versions of the band toured under names like Cro-Mag Jam, Street Justice and Cholo-Mags.

years.h: Revenge reunites Harley Flanagan and Parris Mayhew
years.p: Cro-Mags' first album in seven years, with Harley Flanagan singing and [[Rocky George|ae08bb81-950c-4589-9b9b-9acfbe56b03a]] on lead guitar.

years.h: Parris Mayhew and Harley Flanagan split after the Revenge tour
years.p: The Revenge tour ended with lasting resentment between Mayhew and Flanagan. Through the 1990s and 2000s, Flanagan and John Joseph sometimes ran separate Cro-Mags at the same time.
years.xp:
Per Wikipedia, those parallel versions billed themselves as Cro-Mag Jam, Street Justice, Age of Quarrel, FVK (Fearless Vampire Killers) or Cholo-Mags, each with a completely different line-up.

By 2002–03 even the reunion line-up with John Joseph back on vocals had run out, and the band stopped.

eras.title: Two Cro-Mags, one knife
eras.text: John Joseph and Mackie Jayson put a Cro-Mags back on stage without Harley Flanagan, and the feud turned physical in 2012 and legal in 2018. It ended with one man owning the name.

years.h: John Joseph and Mackie Jayson restart Cro-Mags without Flanagan
years.p: Their line-up adds Craig Setari of [[Sick of It All|e204ed91-3684-4561-b29b-d0b53f8459a7]] on bass and A.J. Novello of [[Leeway|121193a5-cb8b-4182-968c-8ba607856fa2]] on guitar.

years.h: Harley Flanagan is arrested after a knife fight at Webster Hall
years.p: At a show by John Joseph's Cro-Mags, two band members said Flanagan stabbed and bit them backstage. Flanagan said they attacked him in the dressing room and he drew a knife in self-defense.
years.xp: Flanagan's own leg wound took 30 stitches. Prosecutors dropped the criminal charges in December 2012 for lack of cooperating witnesses, and a later civil suit was dismissed.

years.h: John Joseph finishes his first Ironman
years.p: Five weeks after Webster Hall, the Cro-Mags singer completes his first Ironman triathlon. He'd run the Marine Corps Marathon in 2007.

years.h: Original Cro-Mags guitarist Dave Stein dies
years.p: Dave Stein played guitar in Harley Flanagan's first, 1981 version of the band.

years.h: Harley Flanagan publishes Hard-Core: Life of My Own
years.p: Flanagan's memoir comes out on Feral House, alongside a solo album titled Cro-Mags. John Berry, singer in the earliest Cro-Mags, dies the same year.

years.h: Harley Flanagan sues John Joseph and Mackie Jayson over the name
years.p: A federal trademark suit in the Southern District of New York. Flanagan also has major back surgery for a spinal cord injury this year.

years.h: Todd Youth, Cro-Mags' kid bassist, dies at 47
years.p: Todd Youth went on from Cro-Mags to [[Warzone|496da466-68e9-4cbb-9e86-cbb57eda861a]], [[Murphy's Law|4a9fae02-7de0-4cb8-97d7-1fd790d9675e]], [[D Generation|75a14804-749e-4a5a-b445-4388596b760b]] and [[Danzig|8925a01a-8608-411d-a90b-f3a52d061208]], and played with John Joseph in Bloodclot in 2017.

years.h: Settlement: Flanagan owns Cro-Mags, Joseph becomes Cro-Mags JM
years.p: Harley Flanagan keeps exclusive rights to the Cro-Mags name. John Joseph and Mackie Jayson can keep playing, but as Cro-Mags JM.

eras.title: Harley's Cro-Mags
eras.text: With the name settled, Harley Flanagan rebuilt Cro-Mags around himself and put out its first new music in nineteen years. The next fight, over three letters, went to a federal judge too.

years.h: Don't Give In: Cro-Mags' first new music in 19 years
years.p: Three songs, Don't Give In, Drag You Under and No One's Victim, arrive ahead of tour dates with the [[Misfits|936addc3-91aa-49de-8ec0-0dc186de151f]].

years.h: From the Grave 7-inch with Motörhead's Phil Campbell
years.p: [[Motörhead|57961a97-3796-4bf7-9f02-a985a8979ae9]] guitarist Phil Campbell plays on the Cro-Mags single.

years.h: Cro-Mags stream a free show from SIR Studios in lockdown
years.p: One of the first bands to livestream a concert in the early weeks of COVID-19.

years.h: In the Beginning, Cro-Mags' first album in twenty years
years.p: Harley Flanagan's line-up makes the band's sixth studio album.

years.h: A judge ends Cro-Mags JM over a switch to Cro-Mags JAM
years.p: John Joseph's license was revoked after he billed his band as Cro-Mags JAM, and a federal court in New York granted Flanagan a permanent injunction. Joseph said in 2024 he'll never reunite with the classic line-up.

years.h: Harley Flanagan: Wired for Chaos premieres
years.p: A documentary on Flanagan's life. In December he also launches a hot sauce called Age of Hot Sauce.

years.h: Best Wishes drummer Pete Hines rejoins Cro-Mags
years.p: Pete Hines's return sets up the band's first East Coast tour with him in more than 35 years.

years.h: Cro-Mags sign to BLKIIBLK Records
years.p: In June they release Wired for Chaos, their first new song in six years, and announce a new album for 2027.

years.h: Cro-Mags re-record The Age of Quarrel for its 40th
years.p: A full re-recording, scheduled for November 13, previewed by a new World Peace in August. Flanagan said in August he's stepping back from regular touring.
